messages:
alex_cheng: Heads-up — the int8 canary we flipped for v3 is producing a noticeable uptick in malformed JSON for function calls. Parse failures up ~3.8x at ~50 qps. Anyone on this? :warning:

maria_k: Can you paste a raw example from the logs? Is it truncated tokens or extra chars?

alex_cheng: pasted two snippets from the error stream: one truncated JSON and one with trailing garbage.

```

Partial1: {
  "name": "lookup_product",
  "args": {
    "product_id": "B12345",
    "fields": ["title", "price"]
// <-- model stopped mid-token
```

```

Partial2: {"name": "summarize", "args": {"text": "..."}}, \u001b[0m

// trailing escape/garbage
```

samir: Hmm. Could be quantization-induced tokenization shifts causing early EOS emission or bad detokenization for some sequences. Two quick mitigations: 1) short-circuit rescues (small retry w/ repair prompt) and 2) backpressure/circuit-breaker to avoid overwhelming the canary when it misbehaves.

jen_s: +1. Also suggest a lightweight JSON-completeness heuristic before attempting schema parse: check balanced braces, last token not "," or incomplete escape. If borderline, run a small repair_prompt and then re-parse. That avoids full retry of model generation.

maria_k: Can we get concrete config values to test? I'm worried about increasing tail latency with naive retries.

samir: Proposed guard config (P0 experiment):

```
funcall_rescue:
  inflight_limit: 6           # max concurrent requests to canary per route
  retry_policy:
    max_retries: 2
    backoff_ms: [120, 360]
  json_ttl_ms: 180            # if partial json older than this, drop and fail fast
  repair_prompt_enabled: true
  repair_prompt_template: "Please emit only the JSON object that matches the schema. If truncated, close braces and remove trailing junk."
```

jen_s: I like json_ttl concept — prevents accumulating stale partials that then cause cascading retries. Could we also add an early circuit-breaker that trips at 5% parse_error_rate over 2 minutes and reroutes to float32 fallback?

alex_cheng: yes — fallback routing already exists. Decision: when parse_error_rate > 5% for canary model AND inflight queue > 8, route to v2-fp32.

ci-bot: [deploy-bot] Canary deploy 1903456600 -> v3-int8 started. Observability hook: structured-output-parse-rate metric configured.

maria_k: I'll add an eval that runs our 1k structured-output prompts through v2-fp32 and v3-int8 with the rescue logic on/off. Want to measure: parse_success_rate, median_latency, repair_prompt_success_rate.

samir: Add one more metric: repaired_but_incorrect_schema (we need false-positive repairs). Use our schema-checker to mark repairs that pass JSON syntax but fail schema.

jen_s: Suggest we also capture token-level heatmaps for the failure subset to feed into quantization tuning. Might reveal specific tokens that get truncated.

alex_cheng: Action items: @maria_k run the 1k eval (P0) with config above; @samir wire circuit-breaker rule; @jen_s add repair heuristics + token-heatmap logging. I'll throttle canary to 30 qps until we have results. :calendar:

maria_k: On it. ETA 6h for first pass. Will post a short report in this thread when done.

samir: Also adding a short-term metric to Console: per-route parse_failure_rate by model_variant (30s granularity).

jen_s: If repair_prompt improves parse_success by >50% but schema correctness drops >5%, we should disable auto-repair and only surface a repair suggestion in logs for manual triage.

alex_cheng: Agreed. Tight guardrails for auto-repair.

ci-bot: [ci] Alert created: structured-output-parse-rate exceeded threshold for v3-int8 (6.2%) at 1903456732.

alex_cheng: Noted. Will follow up with triage doc and link to the eval results once @maria_k posts them. Thanks all. :pray:
